Draw samples of the edge list from the posterior

Source: R/bison_model.R
draw_edgelist_samples.Rd

Returns randomly chosen posterior draws of all the edge weights. Each draw is one plausible version of the network, consistent with the data. Use it to repeat an analysis in other software on many versions of the network, so the results include the uncertainty in the edge weights.

Usage

draw_edgelist_samples(obj, num_draws, transform = FALSE)

Arguments

obj

A fitted bison_model object.

num_draws

Number of posterior draws to return. Draws are chosen without replacement, unless more are requested than the model has.

transform

If TRUE, edge weights are on the natural scale (probabilities or rates); if FALSE (the default, for backwards compatibility) they're on the link scale (log-odds or log rates).

Value

A data frame with one row per dyad, columns node_1 and node_2, and one column per posterior draw (draw.1, draw.2, ...).

See also

get_edgelist() for a summary of each edge weight, bison_to_igraph() for draws as igraph networks, and extract_metric() for draws of network metrics.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
head(draw_edgelist_samples(fit_edge, num_draws = 3, transform = TRUE))
#>   node_1 node_2    draw.1     draw.2    draw.3
#> 1      1      2 0.2976116 0.03244854 0.6726602
#> 2      1      3 0.8843165 0.18874521 0.8969270
#> 3      1      4 0.1601845 0.43872967 0.4599058
#> 4      1      5 0.2104690 0.73684290 0.6061320
#> 5      1      6 0.8727320 0.46594499 0.3865661
#> 6      1      7 0.7500169 0.90475837 0.4474396
